course_subtitle: Welcome, future programmer, to the journey of moving from blocks to real codes! Here you will write Python commands to animate Toby, create a calculation bot, and draw squares. Open the terminals and write your first real line of code!

stations.title: Station 1: Write your first real Python code
stations.desc: Learn how to replace blocks and write the first print command in real Python.
stations.story: Welcome, future champion, to the world of real codes! You are now grown up and ready to type commands yourself instead of pulling blocks. We use the magic word print to make Python talk.
stations.simple: Like when you grow up and move from pencil to pen! Here we put the blocks in place and start writing real code like great programmers in international companies!
stations.hint: Type in the editor: print("I'm a super little Python programmer") and press Run!
stations.challenge: Print the magic sentence I'm a super little Python programmer to simulate writing code.
stations.starter_code: # Write your first real Python code here:

pills.label: Print the first code
pills.code: print("I'm a super little Python programmer")

validation_rules.required_output_text: I'm a super junior Python programmer

stations.title: Station 2: Animating Toby Bear with codes
stations.desc: Write a Python code to make Tobi the bear move 10 steps forward on the platform!
stations.story: Toby Bear is waiting for your programming commands! Instead of the movement block, we write the line tobi.forward(10) to make Tobi move forward skillfully.
stations.simple: Like a remote control! You write the command to the robot Toby, and he executes it word for word and walks on the stage in front of you!
stations.challenge: Print the magic phrase Toby Bear moves 10 steps forward to simulate the sprite's movement.
stations.starter_code: # Simulate animating Toby Bear with Python code:

stations.title: Station 3: Programming the smart calculation bot
stations.desc: Create a calculation bot that requests two numbers from the user, combines them into a variable (sum), and prints the result immediately!
stations.story: Python loves mathematics! We program the calculation bot to store the first and second numbers in variable bins, then combine them using the + tag and print the result.
stations.simple: Like an automated cashier! You give him the prices and he collects them in a second and gives you the final invoice that is 100% accurate!
stations.hint: Type total = 30 + 40 and then print("The sum of the two numbers is:", total).
stations.challenge: Create a variable `total = 30 + 40` and print the statement `The sum of the two numbers is: 70` on the screen.
stations.starter_code: # Simulate an intelligent calculation bot in Python:

pills.label: Calculate and print the total
pills.code:
total = 30 + 40
print("The sum of the two numbers is:", total)

validation_rules.required_output_text: The sum of the two numbers is: 70

stations.title: Station 4: Draw the box with the loop
stations.desc: Use a for loop to make Python repeat the move and wrap command 4 times to draw a square!
stations.story: The smart programmer saves the lines! Instead of typing the motion command 4 times to draw the box, we use the for i in range(4): loop to do the work for us.
stations.simple: Like a ferris wheel! You wind 4 turns and each roll draws an edge until it completes the beautiful square!
stations.hint: Type for i in range(4): and below it with a space print("Draw the side of the square").
stations.challenge: Use the loop to print square side plot 4 times in a row.
stations.starter_code: # Simulate drawing a box with a for loop:

pills.label: Square drawing ring
pills.code:
for i in range(4):
    print("Draw the side of the square")

required_keywords: Draw a side of a square
Draw a side of a square
Draw a side of a square
Draw a side of a square

stations.title: Station 5: Apple hunting game with codes
stations.desc: Program a falling apple catch game using Python commands and make the score variable subtly increment!
stations.story: Game programming becomes more exciting with codes! We program the apple to fall down (change Y), and we program the basket to move left and right, and upon contact we increase the points.
stations.simple: Like the famous Atari games! You move on Saturday under the apple that falls and collect the most points!
stations.hint: Type print("The apple is caught and code points are increased").
stations.challenge: Print the magic sentence The apple was caught and code points increased to simulate the game.
stations.starter_code: # Apple hunting game simulation in Python:

pills.label: Apple hunting
pills.code: print("The apple was caught and the code points increased")

validation_rules.required_output_text: The apple was caught and the code points increased

stations.title: Stop 6: Grand Prix Race Game
stations.desc: The grand final stop! Programming a street car racing and obstacle avoidance game using the real Python language!
stations.story: The big final stop in Python for little ones! We will program a car racing game. We control the hero's car with arrows, generate random cars and barriers on the road, and whoever passes them wins the trophy!
stations.simple: Like car racing games in amusement parks! You drive and avoid other cars coming your way in order to reach the finish line and win the race!
stations.hint: Type print("The grand car racing game has been played and the little hero has won!").
stations.challenge: Print the closing statement The grand car racing game has been played and the little hero has won! to celebrate the completion of your first full Python game!
stations.starter_code: # Car racing game running simulation conclusion:

pills.label: Run car race
pills.code: print("The grand car racing game has been played and the little hero has won!")

validation_rules.required_output_text: The grand car racing game is on and the little hero wins!
